neighbours.label: A light-sensing imaging chip (CCD, image sensor, the pixels of a detector), vs sensors and detectors that do not form images
fire: Amateur astronomers often bolt a CCD to the back of a small telescope.
Inside the flatbed scanner, a CCD records each line of the page as it passes.
The space telescope's focal plane is tiled with more than a hundred CCDs.
Dust on the image sensor shows up as dark spots in every photo I take.
The lab cooled the CCD chip with liquid nitrogen to cut thermal noise.
Every pixel on the CCD collects charge in proportion to the light it receives.
This mirrorless camera has a larger image sensor than last year's model.
The microscope sends its picture to a CCD camera mounted above the eyepiece.
quiet: Amateur astronomers often bolt a filter wheel to the back of a small telescope.
Inside the flatbed scanner, a roller moves the page forward line by line.
The space telescope's main mirror is tiled with eighteen gold hexagons.
Dust on the kitchen shelf shows up as grey fuzz every few weeks.
The lab cooled the motor with liquid nitrogen to cut wear on the bearings.
Every pressure sensor on the pipeline reports a reading once a minute.
This thermostat has a better humidity sensor than last year's model.
The hallway smoke detector beeps whenever someone burns the toast.

predictions: CCD and image-sensor sentences 0.3-0.8; smoke detectors, pressure or humidity sensors and plain telescope parts under 0.1.
notes: Card: ' CCD' x7, ' detector' x5, ' sensor' x4 in optics/astronomy. Probe: cooled CCD camera 0.748, CCD frame 0.353, phone image sensor 0.420, photodetector 0.312, Pixels 0.287; smoke detector 0.013, temperature sensor 0.035, telescope long exposure 0.154. The distinction is imaging vs non-imaging sensing.
